updates.title: MA zoning reform: variance standard replaced with 'practical difficulty'
updates.summary: The FY2027 state budget (signed July 9, 2026, effective immediately) amended G.L. c.40A section 10, retiring the 40-year-old 'substantial hardship' variance test tied to a lot's unique soil, shape, or topography. Boards may now grant a variance on a showing of 'practical difficulty,' and financial hardship plus housing benefit are explicit factors. This is the most consequential change to MA zoning practice in four decades.
updates.action: Revisit any fix-and-flip, conversion, or density project previously denied a variance under the old standard - several may now clear the bar. Raise the new standard with counsel before the next ZBA filing.

updates.title: MA $1M+ real estate transfer withholding remains a closing requirement
updates.summary: Massachusetts requires withholding at closing on real estate transfers at or above the $1,000,000 threshold, effective Nov 1, 2025. The obligation sits with the closing process, so it surfaces late and can strand seller proceeds if nobody has planned for it. It applies across the real estate and lending sides of the portfolio.
updates.action: Confirm closing attorneys are collecting and remitting on every disposition at or above $1M, and that estimated-tax positions account for amounts already withheld so the portfolio does not overpay twice.

updates.title: MA Commercial Conversion Tax Credit: $15.3M awarded for 856 new homes
updates.summary: The Healey administration, through EOHLC, awarded $15.3M under the Commercial Conversion Tax Credit Initiative to convert commercial buildings into 856 new housing units. The awards confirm the CCTCI pipeline is funding real conversions rather than sitting unused. The 2026 NOFA round closed April 2, 2026.
updates.action: Watch for the next NOFA cycle before committing 159 Main St (Cooper's Commons) or 939 East Columbus Ave to a conversion plan - the credit materially changes the pro forma and the application window drives the schedule.

updates.title: MA FY2027 budget signed - no new taxes or fees
updates.summary: Governor Healey signed the $63.4B FY2027 budget on July 9, 2026 with no vetoes and no new taxes or fees. Roughly $2.7B in Fair Share surtax revenue is allocated 64% to education and 36% to transportation. Separately, FY2026 surtax collections came in near $3.1B against a $2B projection, making the surtax a durable core budget item and lowering the odds of repeal.
updates.action: No filing action. Plan on the 4% surtax being permanent for modeling purposes rather than treating it as a temporary overlay.

updates.title: MA H.5470: elective PTET expanded to cover the 4% surtax
updates.summary: The FY26 supplemental budget (enacted June 12, 2026) expanded the elective pass-through entity tax to cover the 4% surtax beginning in TY2026. An electing S-corp or partnership can pay the surtax portion at the entity level, making it federally deductible without regard to the SALT cap, with members claiming the usual 90% MA credit. The same act delayed MA conformity to the OBBBA section 179, R&D, and section 163(j) provisions behind revenue triggers, so federal and state books can diverge.
updates.action: Have the CPA model a 2026 PTET election including the surtax before the Q3 estimate due September 15. The election is made per entity annually - confirm which entities benefit. Flag the conformity delay so MA depreciation and interest add-backs are not a filing-season surprise.

updates.title: IRS Notice 2026-11: interim guidance on permanent 100% bonus depreciation
updates.summary: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act permanently restored 100% first-year bonus depreciation for qualified property acquired after January 19, 2025, eliminating the scheduled phase-down. IRS Notice 2026-11, issued January 14, 2026, provides interim guidance and confirms treatment for cost-segregated components of rental acquisitions and for equipment. Notice 2026-16 (February 20, 2026) extends 100% treatment to Qualified Production Property.
updates.action: Run cost segregation on acquisitions above roughly $500K before year-end and coordinate with the CPA on which entity claims the deduction. Remember MA conformity is delayed under H.5470, so the state add-back is real.

updates.title: QOZ deferred gains become taxable Dec 31, 2026; OZ 2.0 nominations open
updates.summary: All pre-2027 gains deferred into Qualified Opportunity Funds are recognized on 2026 returns. IRS Notice 2026-40 (June 18, 2026) confirms the December 31, 2026 deemed inclusion, preserves the 10-year FMV step-up on exit, and adds working-capital and ordinary-course-replacement safe harbors plus a compliance bridge through 2047. Separately, the OZ 2.0 nomination window is open: MA will designate 103 zones from 410 eligible tracts, with state nominations due September 28, 2026 and designations effective January 1, 2027.
updates.action: Plan liquidity now for the December 31 inclusion - holdings of 5+ years get a 10% exclusion and 7+ years get 15%. Review the published MA eligible-tract map against target submarkets and submit feedback before the Healey administration's early-September submission.

updates.title: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act signed - institutional investor moratorium
updates.summary: H.R. 6644 became law July 11, 2026 (Senate 85-5, House 358-32), the first major bipartisan federal housing package since the 1990s. It imposes a broad moratorium on large institutional investors purchasing single-family homes and adds supply-side reforms covering zoning incentives, permitting, and manufactured housing. Final text softened the build-to-rent provisions: the 7-year forced-disposal requirement and the renter right-of-first-refusal were dropped.
updates.action: The moratorium targets large institutional buyers, not portfolios of this size - no direct restriction expected. Track the supply-side incentives, which may open permitting and zoning advantages worth using.

updates.title: CFPB eliminates ECOA disparate-impact liability; MA authority survives
updates.summary: The CFPB's rewrite of Regulation B took effect July 21, 2026, eliminating disparate-impact liability under ECOA at the federal level. Massachusetts, along with California and New Jersey, retains independent state-level disparate-impact authority, so MA compliance posture is essentially unchanged. For the lending business the business-purpose exemption remains the operative shield.
updates.action: No change to underwriting or fair-lending documentation for MA lending. Do not treat the federal rollback as relief from state exposure.

updates.title: MA deeds excise proposed for transfers of controlling interests
updates.summary: A pending proposal would extend the MA deeds excise to entity-level transfers - transfers of LLC or TIC interests holding MA real property, not just recorded deeds - with a $1M cap on the assumed-mortgage deduction. This is still a proposal and not law, but it would reach structures that currently transfer outside the recording system.
updates.action: Directly relevant to the Flying Monkey TIC (1361 Memorial Dr) and the 59 King Spring TIC structure. If any interest transfer is contemplated, discuss timing with counsel before the proposal advances.

updates.title: MA SJC strikes rent control question from the November 2026 ballot
updates.summary: The Supreme Judicial Court ruled on June 23, 2026 that the statewide rent control initiative cannot appear on the November 2026 ballot; the petition's religious-institution exemption was held unconstitutional. 88,132 signatures had been certified. Supporters plan to refile. A separate rent stabilization bill remains before a joint committee.
updates.action: No rent caps this cycle - continue market-rate rent-setting across all management entities. Keep the rent stabilization bill on the watch list rather than treating the risk as closed.

updates.title: MA MRVP/AHVP voucher rent increase rules effective July 1, 2026
updates.summary: For MRVP and AHVP voucher tenants, rent increases may now be taken only at lease renewal and must be requested at least 90 days in advance. Requests submitted fewer than 60 days out are deferred to the following year, meaning a missed window costs a full year of increase.
updates.action: Calendar 90-day notice deadlines for every voucher-tenant lease anniversary and build the reminder into the renewal workflow so no increase is lost to timing.

updates.title: MA PFAS bills and Mass Ready Act still live after the July 31 session date
updates.summary: The Legislature's July 31 formal session 'deadline' is not a hard stop. The roughly $120M PFAS remediation bond bill (Mass Ready Act) and the PFAS consumer-product ban bills (S.1504/H.2197, with a biosolids land-application ban in S.2802) remain in conference committee, and once conferees are named talks can continue informally into the fall and winter. Separately, EPA draft guidance on PFOA/PFOS in biosolids walks back the prior risk assessment as overstated, signaling a lighter-touch federal posture.
updates.action: No action required. Do not expect quick resolution on either bill; revisit carwash discharge and chemical sourcing exposure if the consumer-product ban moves.

updates.title: IRS mid-year mileage rate increase to 76 cents per mile
updates.summary: IRB 2026-29 raised the business standard mileage rate from 72.5 cents to 76 cents per mile effective July 1, 2026 - the first mid-year adjustment since 2022. Trips before and after July 1 must be rated separately.
updates.action: Split 2026 mileage logs at July 1 and update any reimbursement templates or bookkeeping rules that hardcode the old rate.
